tools.name: politics_represent
tools.description: Representation lookup for a US ZIP code: both U.S. Senators, the U.S. House member for that ZIP's congressional district, and the state's statewide executives (governor, attorney general, and similar). Every official carries source_url (the capture origin) and source_link (a public page).

tools.name: politics_search
tools.description: Search for politicians and elected officials across all levels of US government — federal, state, county, municipal. Filter by name, state, party, level, chamber, or office title. Returns officials with their current office, party, and contact info.

office.description: Office title (e.g. Senator, Mayor, Governor, Town Clerk)

tools.name: politics_official
tools.description: Get full details for a specific official by ID — biography, party, office, policy positions, committee assignments, campaign finance, social media, and contact info. All data includes source URLs for verification.

bioguide_id.description: Congress.gov Bioguide ID (e.g. S000033 for Bernie Sanders)

positions_limit.description: Max policy positions to return (default 15, max 250). Response is bounded so it fits any AI client tool-result limit.

positions_offset.description: Pagination offset for positions (page with offset += limit).

expand.description: Return the fuller record (larger response, untruncated detail). Default false = bounded for AI consumption.

tools.name: politics_resolve
tools.description: Resolve a messy name string (e.g. "Rep. Johnson", "cornyn") to a canonical official — returns the best match with a 0-1 confidence score and ranked alternatives. Use this first when you have a name but not an ID; then call politics_official with best.id. Add state to disambiguate.

name.description: Name to resolve (partial/with title/lowercase all OK)

tools.name: politics_by_state
tools.description: Get all current officials for a US state — federal senators and representatives, state legislators, and any indexed local officials. Organized by government level.

tools.name: politics_positions
tools.description: Policy positions across officials by topic, covering who supports or opposes issues such as crypto, stablecoins, AI, healthcare, and guns. Each position carries a source URL and origin hash. Returns compact records by default (id, name, party, state, stance, summary, source) with a total count; the compact parameter controls row detail and offset controls paging.

topic.description: Policy topic label — use exact stored labels: Cryptocurrency, Technology, Healthcare, Immigration, Climate, Gun Control, Abortion, Taxes, Economy, Education, National Security, Housing, Criminal Justice, Social Security, Voting Rights, Agriculture, Trade

compact.description: Compact mode (default). Small bounded record per position; use with offset to page. Set false for full rows (limit capped at 50).

offset.description: Pagination offset. Response includes total; page by offset += limit.

limit.description: Max results per page. Compact: default 100, max 250. Full: default 25, max 50.

tools.name: politics_stats
tools.description: Get summary statistics for the politics.rootz.global database — total officials, breakdown by level, party, state, and chamber. Shows coverage completeness.

tools.name: politics_timeline
tools.description: Get the full origin timeline for a politician — every page snapshot, every position change, every data source with hash proof. The political wayback machine. Shows what changed, when, and where the data came from.

tools.name: politics_election_2026
tools.description: Status of the 2026 general election record: official results sources captured per state, the pre-election baseline, and how fresh each collection is. Counts are unofficial until a state certifies; this service never calls a race. Pass official_id to get what that official's pages said just before the polls opened.

official_id.description: Optional official ID: return that official's election-eve excerpts

tools.name: politics_changes
tools.description: Get recent changes detected across all politicians: sentences added to or removed from their pages, and pages that changed HTTP status. Each change names the archived records it compares. Topics say what a sentence mentions, never what stance it takes.

since.description: ISO date to filter changes after (e.g. 2026-05-01)

tools.name: politics_origin
tools.description: Get origin archive statistics — total snapshots, changes detected, origin proofs recorded, unique URLs tracked. Shows the depth of the political wayback machine.

tools.name: politics_bridge_create
tools.description: Create a citizen bridge page — a personalized workspace for tracking representatives, comparing positions, and taking action (write letters, log calls). Returns a shareable URL that any AI agent can collaborate on. Optionally auto-populates with the citizen's state representatives.

zip.description: ZIP code for precise district matching

tools.name: politics_bridge_session
tools.description: Current state of a citizen bridge workspace: tracked officials, saved comparisons, drafted actions, and messages.

agent_id.description: Your agent identifier for multi-agent tracking

tools.name: politics_bridge_compare
tools.description: Compare multiple politicians side-by-side on a bridge page — positions, party, office, campaign finance. Optionally filter to a specific topic.

official_ids.description: Array of official IDs to compare

topic.description: Optional topic to focus comparison on

tools.name: politics_bridge_letter
tools.description: Draft a letter to a politician on the citizen's bridge page. The letter gets an origin hash for proof of content. Returns delivery options (email, web form, USPS, phone).

tools.name: politics_bill
tools.description: Details of a US bill or resolution: vote breakdown, sponsors, cosponsors, status, and origin proof. Returns metadata, a short text excerpt, and a text index by default; full legislative text is omitted because omnibus bills exceed typical token caps. The include_text parameter controls whether the complete text is returned in a single response.

bill_id.description: Bill ID (e.g. hr3424-119 for House bill 3424 in 119th Congress)

include_text.description: excerpt (default): metadata + ~1.2KB head + text index. none: metadata + index only. full: entire full_text (may exceed the token cap for large bills).

tools.name: politics_bill_toc
tools.description: Section index for a bill: every "SEC. N" heading with its character offset and length, plus the whole-bill origin hash (content_hash) and total text length. A small response that describes the structure of a large bill.

tools.name: politics_bill_text
tools.description: One signed, bounded slice of a bill's full legislative text, addressed by part number or section label. Each response carries part and total_parts, next_part, the slice's part_sha256, and the whole-bill content_hash. Parts 1 through total_parts concatenated in order hash to content_hash, so a bill too large to return in a single response remains verifiable as complete and unaltered.

part.description: 1-based part number. Response tells you total_parts and next_part.

section.description: Jump to a section by label instead of part, e.g. "2", "SEC. 2", or "preamble". Overrides part.

max_chars.description: Max characters per part (2000–60000). Larger = fewer parts but bigger responses.

tools.name: politics_bills_search
tools.description: Search bills by topic, sponsor, status, or congress. Returns bill metadata and whether full text is available.

status.description: Bill status: introduced, committee, passed_house, passed_senate, enacted

tools.name: politics_candidate_feed
tools.description: Get a candidate's Campaign Data Standard (CDS) feed: a single machine-readable record of who they are, the offices they hold and seek, their positions in their own words (each source-linked), their voting record by reference, and declared data gaps. This is the standardized, signed feed an AI or reporter uses to grab a candidate's positions and verify they are genuine. Every MCP response is signed; the standalone signed feed is also at /official/{id}/candidate.json. Tier is "rootz-compiled" until the campaign claims and signs it ("candidate-signed").

positions_limit.description: Max positions in the delivered feed (default 15, max 500). The complete signed feed (all positions) is always at signed_feed_url.

expand.description: Deliver more positions inline (larger response). Default false = bounded for AI consumption.

tools.name: politics_alignment
tools.description: Compare an official's stated positions against their actual roll-call votes, per topic — what they SAY vs how they VOTED, both source-linked. Does NOT label agreement/contradiction (you judge and cite); surfaces the juxtaposition no unsigned source can. Use official id.

tools.name: politics_coverage
tools.description: Coverage map: per-state, per-dataset completeness (officials by level, positions, finance, state-legislative votes). Shows WHERE the data is deep (federal — complete) vs sparse (local). Use it to know whether silence means "no data captured" rather than "nothing there".

tools.name: politics_methodology
tools.description: Get the full transparency methodology — how we collect, assess, extract, sign, and verify political data. Includes quality assessment algorithm (signals + weights), trust levels, data sources, cron schedule, and what we can and cannot prove. Open and auditable.

tools.name: politics_provenance
tools.description: Get the complete origin proof chain for an official — every data source, content hash, quality assessment, snapshot history, and verification instructions. Proves where every piece of data came from.

tools.name: politics_speeches
tools.description: Search Congressional Record floor speeches by official, topic, date range, or keyword. Returns verbatim text from the official government record with origin proof hash. Every speech is directly citable with a GPO source URL.

bioguide_id.description: Bioguide ID (e.g. L000571 for Lummis, S001184 for Tim Scott)

tools.name: politics_candidates
tools.description: Registered federal candidates for the 2026 election cycle, filterable by state, office (senate, house, president), party, or presence of a campaign URL. Returns campaign website, social media links, FEC data, and position and speech counts.

state.description: Two-letter state code (e.g. ME, CA, TX)

party.description: Filter by party (Democrat, Republican, Libertarian, etc.)

has_url.description: Only return candidates with campaign websites

tools.name: politics_state_votes
tools.description: Search state legislature votes across 26+ US states. Filter by state, topic, or date. Returns bill title, vote result, yes/no counts.

state.description: Two-letter state code (CA, TX, NY, etc.)

tools.name: politics_municipalities
tools.description: Search US municipalities (cities, towns, villages, counties). Every incorporated place in the US with coordinates. Filter by state, name, or type. Returns website, platform, meeting calendar, and board/commission info where available.

state.description: Two-letter state code (MA, CA, TX, etc.)

type.description: Place type: city, town, village, borough, county, cdp

tools.name: politics_create_watchlist
tools.description: Creates a Just the Facts watchlist bound to an email address, covering any combination of specific officials, issue topics, and a town with state for local meetings, agendas, and minutes. Sends a double-opt-in confirmation email and returns the bridge workspace URL.

town.description: Town/city to track local meetings (e.g. Fort Myers)

report_prompt.description: Plain-English brief for how the digest is written

tools.name: politics_polls
tools.description: Search the SIGNED public-poll archive. Unlike aggregators, every poll keeps the EXACT question wording, population base (LV/RV/adults), sample size, margin of error, mode, and per-option toplines — first-party sourced, snapshot-hashed, and cryptographically signed (verifiable). Filter by race_key, state, subject (e.g. "approval", "Senate"), pollster, or since (ISO date). Returns a list; call politics_poll {id} for full detail + signature. Use this when a question hinges on what a poll ACTUALLY asked vs how it was reported.

race_key.description: Stable contest key to get every poll of one race over time (e.g. us-pres-approval-trump)

since.description: Only polls whose field_end >= this ISO date (e.g. 2026-08-01)

tools.name: politics_poll
tools.description: Get one poll in full: pollster, sponsor, field dates, population, sample size, margin of error, mode, the VERBATIM question(s) asked, per-option toplines, the first-party source_url, and the signature (poll_proof) that binds the exact wording and numbers. This is the ground truth to check any claim about a poll against.
